text: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE · QUANTUM CHEMISTRY · DFT Quantum chemistry and DFT: approximations and equations From Schrödinger, HF and DFT to bases, SCF and correlation, including space groups, little-group irreps, SOC and time reversal in band calculations. Bilingual reading for 20 entries and 36 primary publications. Runnable validation covers two hydrogenic/He families and scoped finite-basis H₂ RHF. A fixed periodic-He LDA workflow is also available; general molecular DFT and other periodic materials remain unvalidated. Three choices to keep separate Physical model and approximation HF, KS-DFT, MP2, CI or CC: which many-electron states and energies are approximated? Representation and discretization Basis, grid, pseudopotential and k sampling: how is the model made finite? Equation solver Eigensolvers, SCF, mixing and DIIS: how accurately is the chosen discrete problem solved? SCF convergence, basis convergence and physical adequacy are distinct checks. Representative equations use atomic units (ℏ = m_e = e = 4πε₀ = 1). Finite molecules and periodic solids also require different boundaries. Schrodinger eigenproblems The common starting point is a many-electron eigenproblem at fixed nuclear positions. We use nonrelativistic Born–Oppenheimer theory and atomic units, separating electronic energy E_el from nuclear repulsion E_NN. R_A and Z_A denote nuclear positions and charges; r_ij is an electron–electron distance. For one electron the pair-repulsion sum vanishes; hydrogenic energies E_n = −Z²/(2n²) provide references. The many-electron wavefunction depends on all electronic coordinates and spins, unlike the individual three-dimensional orbitals in HF or KS. Uniform radial-grid tests of isolated hydrogenic 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d states; not a direct general many-electron Schrödinger solver. (1929) Band symmetry groups and irreducible representations A structural space group includes translations, rotations, mirrors, inversion and their combinations. Band classification must use the symmetries actually preserved by the Hamiltonian, including magnetic order, spin–orbit coupling (SOC) and external fields. A Seitz operation g = {R|τ} maps position to Rr + τ. With lattice translations T as a normal subgroup, G/T is the crystal point group. At each k, the little group G_k retains operations taking Rk back to k modulo a reciprocal vector K. Its little co-group G_k/T is distinct from the full crystal point group. g={R∣τ}: r↦Rr+τ,P=G/Tg={R∣τ}: r↦Rr+τ,P=G/TGk={{R∣τ}∈G: Rk=k+K, K∈L∗}Gk​={{R∣τ}∈G: Rk=k+K, K∈L∗} Long equations scroll horizontally. Read little-group irreps and degeneracies Symmetries act within the Bloch-state space associated with k. Irreducible small representations classify bands. Their dimensions constrain symmetry-required multiplicities; accidental coincidence and antiunitary pairing are additional possibilities. Nearly equal energies alone do not identify an irrep. Little groups change between high-symmetry points, lines and planes. Compatibility relations track representation branching and band connectivity. For a simple symmorphic mirror line without SOC, mirror eigenvalues +1 and −1 label distinct sectors that cannot hybridize while that symmetry is preserved. Screw axes, glide planes and nonsymmorphic groups Screw and glide operations include fractional translations. Bloch phases matter, particularly at zone boundaries, so ordinary crystal-point-group character tables are insufficient. Use little-group small representations or equivalent projective little-co-group representations with their factor systems. Nonsymmorphic symmetry can constrain degeneracies and connectivity. It does not imply that every band is degenerate at every k: specify the group, k, spin and time-reversal conditions. ψnk(r+a)=eik⋅aψnk(r),a∈Lψnk​(r+a)=eik⋅aψnk​(r),a∈L SOC, double groups, time reversal and Kramers pairs Spin-1/2 SOC requires spinors that change sign under a 2π rotation, hence double-valued representations of double groups. Time reversal Θ is antiunitary with Θ² = −1 for electrons. Time reversal alone generally pairs k with −k; Kramers degeneracy at the same k is guaranteed at time-reversal-invariant momenta (TRIM), where 2k is reciprocal. In the usual nonmagnetic spin-1/2 setting with both inversion P and time reversal Θ, PΘ preserves each k and squares to −1, producing double degeneracy at each k. This conclusion cannot be transferred unchanged to a noncentrosymmetric system. Spinless Θ² = +1 models also do not satisfy these Kramers assumptions. Magnetic order may break time reversal or retain only its combination with a spatial operation. Magnetic space groups and antiunitary corepresentations require separate treatment. Reassess symmetry settings whenever SOC or magnetic state changes.
